title: Automatic Spatio-Temporal Kriging
text: Automatic spatio-temporal variogram fitting autofitVariogramST(). Automatic spatio-temporal Kriging autoKrigeST(). Explicit fit/predict workflow fitVariogramST() predictKrigeST(). Cross-validation autoKrigeST.cv() using spatial, temporal, spatio-temporal, random folds. Support STFDF, STSDF, STIDF, sftime, cubble inputs main fitting prediction workflow. Conversion helper cubble_to_sftime() nested temporal cubble objects. Multiple spatio-temporal variogram structures, including sumMetric, metric, productSum, separable. Multiple optimizers, including lbfgsb, grid, sa, ga.

title: Automatic Spatio-Temporal Kriging
text: autofitVariogramST(): automatically fits spatio-temporal variogram. fitVariogramST(): fits variogram returns reusable STVariogramFit object. predictKrigeST(): predicts fitted STVariogramFit object. autoKrigeST(): fits variogram predicts one call. autoKrigeST.cv(): cross-validates spatio-temporal Kriging results. cubble_to_sftime(): converts cubble_df objects sftime.

what: Forecast Air Quality From Station Networks
title: Automatic Spatio-Temporal Kriging
text: Use autoKrigeST() repeated measurements monitoring stations want predictions future spatio-temporal grid. classic STFDF/STSDF workflow.
code: library(autoSTK) library(gstat) library(sp) library(spacetime) library(stars)  data(air)  deair <- STFDF(stations, dates, data.frame(PM10 = as.vector(air))) deair_sf <- st_as_stars(deair) |>   st_transform("+proj=longlat +ellps=sphere") |>   st_transform(3857)  deair_r <- as(deair_sf, "STFDF") deair_r@sp@proj4string <- CRS(   "+proj=merc +a=6378137 +b=6378137 +lat_ts=0 +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +k=1 +units=m +nadgrids=@null +wktext +no_defs +type=crs" )  deair_rs <- deair_r[, 3701:3800] deair_rss <- as(deair_rs, "STSDF")  akst_stk <- autoKrigeST(   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   input_data = deair_rss,   cutoff = 300000,   width = 30000,   type_stv = "sumMetric",   model = c("Exc", "Mat", "Ste", "Exp", "Wav"),   tlags = 0:7,   cores = 8,   optimizer = "sa",   verbose = TRUE )  akst_stk_stars <- st_as_stars(akst_stk$krige_output) plot(akst_stk_stars[1, ])

title: Automatic Spatio-Temporal Kriging
text: Use sftime data already lives sf-style workflow one geometry column one time column. autoKrigeST() accepts sftime training data prediction data. fitVariogramST() predictKrigeST() useful want reuse fitted variogram across several prediction grids.
code: library(autoSTK) library(sf) library(sftime)  # station_long has columns: #   id, time, PM10, geometry # where geometry is an sfc_POINT column and time is Date/POSIXct. station_sf <- st_as_sf(   station_long,   sf_column_name = "geometry",   crs = 3857 )  station_st <- st_as_sftime(   station_sf,   time_column_name = "time",   sf_column_name = "geometry" )  fit <- fitVariogramST(   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   data = station_st,   typestv = "sumMetric",   candidate_model = c("Sph", "Exp", "Gau", "Ste"),   cutoff = 300000,   width = 30000,   tlags = 0:7 )  pred <- predictKrigeST(   fit = fit,   data = station_st,   newdata = prediction_grid_st,   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   nmax = 40 )

title: Automatic Spatio-Temporal Kriging
text: Use cubble workflow stores station metadata spatial face repeated measurements temporal face. autoSTK can convert either nested temporal face sftime. can also pass cubble_df directly main Kriging workflow supplying prediction grid: cross-validation, convert cubble sftime data spacetime object first, autoKrigeST.cv() builds folds @sp @time slots.
code: library(autoSTK) library(cubble)  # cb is a cubble_df created from an sf object with station geometries and a # temporal table containing PM10 observations. pm10_st <- cubble_to_sftime(cb, time_col = "time", key_col = "id")  akst_cb <- autoKrigeST(   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   input_data = pm10_st,   cutoff = 300000,   width = 30000,   tlags = 0:7,   type_stv = "sumMetric" ) akst_cb <- autoKrigeST(   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   input_data = cb,   new_data = prediction_grid_st,   cutoff = 300000,   width = 30000,   tlags = 0:7 ) pm10_stfdf <- as(as(pm10_st, "STIDF"), "STFDF")  akst_cv_cb <- autoKrigeST.cv(   formula = PM10 ~ 1,   data = pm10_stfdf,   nfold = 3,   fold_dim = "temporal",   cutoff = 300000,   width = 30000,   tlags = 0:7 )

Summarise cross-validation results compare model settings: Lower RMSE MAE indicate smaller prediction errors. title: Cross-validation of spatiotemporal Kriging — autoKrigeST.cv
text: data `STFDF`-class object fold_dim character. dimension want cross-validate (spatial, temporal, random) nfold integer. number folds. 10 default formula formula. e.g., y~1 type_stv character. One 'sumMetric', 'metric', 'productSum', 'separable' block numeric. passed conduct block spatiotemporal Kriging. model character vector. Default c("Sph", "Exp", "Gau", "Ste"), users can specify list theoretical variograms referring gstat::vgm. kappa numeric vector. Kappa values tested Matern-family variogram models. fix.values numeric vector. Initial values order nugget, range, sill, respectively. tlags integer vector (increasing, preferably consecutive). temporal lags. cutoff numeric. maximum distance sample variogram computed. width numeric. interval variogram cloud summarized. nmax integer positive infinite. maximum number spatiotemporal neighbors conduct local spatiotemporal Kriging. aniso_method character. One 'vgm', 'linear', 'range', 'metric'. Please refer ?gstat::estiStAni. type_joint character. model form joint spatiotemporal variogram. prodsum_k numeric. parameter case 'productSum' chosen type_stv. start_vals numeric vector (3). initial values optimize spatiotemporal variogram model. miscFitOptions list. See ?automap::autofitVariogram. cores integer. number threads used compute sample spatiotemporal variogram. newdata_mode character. One 'rect' (rectangular grid) 'chull' (convex hull) newdata_npoints integer. number points generated range geometry user specified (one rectangle convex hull) GLS.model variogram model. default value NA. variogram model passed, Generalized Lease Squares sample variogram calculated. predict_chunk integer. number data points per chunk new data large data. meticulously chosen according user's machine specification.
